clue.text: A few circling wagon have initially found their target

indicators.note: the words for a few go round the wagon and the letter that follows it

parts.note: some means a few
a truck is a goods wagon on the railway

indicators.note: only the opening letter of have is taken

parts.note: its first letter is the one taken

explanation.surface: Pioneers drawing their wagons into a circle have at last hit what they were aiming for.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike home is an idiom for hitting the mark or having the intended effect.

clue.text: Small edge goes to fielder

parts.note: a lip is a rim or edge

explanation.surface: A thin edge off the bat flies to a cricket fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: Slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper, where edged balls tend to go.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a slip is a catching fielder stationed close to the batsman, beside the keeper.

clue.text: Keep going round for a light lunch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to keep turning over
second meaning: a bread ..., a small midday meal

explanation.surface: Someone circles about, hunting for a bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for rotating continuously and a noun for a small loaf eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Hurry up selected pupils to start working regularly

parts.note: come on is said to urge someone to be quick
a stream is a group of pupils sorted by ability

explanation.surface: A teacher urges a chosen set of pupils to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: To come on stream is an idiom for going into regular operation or production.

clue.text: Turner's affair, heading off to Spain

definitions.note: read as Turner is: a hinge is the thing a door turns on

indicators.note: the word for affair drops its first letter

parts.note: a thing is an affair or fling

explanation.surface: The painter Turner's romance, its lead removed, heads off to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter, but it is anything that turns. E is the international vehicle code for Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is the pivot on which a door or lid swings, so it is literally a turner.

clue.text: Shabby way of working not right to challenge

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

indicators.note: the right letter is taken out of the challenge word

parts.note: to threaten is to challenge or menace

explanation.surface: A shabby method, and no right to object.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten describes clothes damaged by moths, and so anything worn out or shabby.

clue.text: Eminent school in street slightly tainted

definitions.meaning: first meaning: exalted, of elevated rank
second meaning: the word that goes before both school and street (... School, ... Street)
third meaning: of meat or game, beginning to go off

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings run together: the middle one is the word that can precede both school and street. Game hung until it smells strong is called high.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers elevated rank, the main road or senior school of a town, and meat starting to turn.

clue.text: Innate bias to be reviewed, when convicted so?

indicators.note: the letters of innate bias are looked over again and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A defendant's inborn prejudice is reexamined after sentence passed without them.
explanation.definitionFit: In absentia means in one's absence, as with someone tried and sentenced without attending court.

clue.text: Rash and blot spread into eyes so half-closed

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for half-shut eyes

parts.note: hooded eyes have drooping lids

indicators.note: the letters of blot are spread out into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A skin rash and a blot spread across sleepy, drooping eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' reads as a skin complaint, but it is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-blooded means passionate and impetuous, which fits rash in the sense of acting without thought.

clue.text: Wise guys' initial gathering around chimney

definitions.note: plural possessive: the clue reads as what the wise guys' initial gathering was

indicators.note: the reworked letters sit around the chimney word
the letters of initial are gathered up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney

explanation.surface: The founding meeting of some clever people happened round a fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initial' looks like it means first meeting, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Illuminati were a secret society of supposedly enlightened people, so the name is used for those claiming special wisdom.

clue.text: Very large piece of meat saved to take back

indicators.note: the hidden fragment is then read in the opposite direction
only a fragment of the words meat saved is used, straddling the gap

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of meat and the start of saved

explanation.surface: Someone is told to retrieve the chunk of meat that was set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast is a direct synonym of huge or immense.

clue.text: As eldest child, male, I severely criticise Dad

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
taken as written
to rap is to rebuke sharply
a dad is a parent

explanation.surface: A first-born son confesses to harshly attacking his father.
explanation.definitionFit: The heir apparent is the one whose right to inherit is certain, traditionally the eldest son.

clue.text: Change in personal relations suggesting trap?

definitions.meaning: the straight sense: people swapping their usual parts in a relationship
cryptically, a role is a part, and part with its letters reversed spells trap

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read as an instruction: take a word for role, reverse it, and you get trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A role reversal is when two people swap their customary positions, such as a parent being cared for by a child.

clue.text: An element of pressure over revised shop hours

indicators.note: in a down answer, the pressure letter sits above the rest
the letters of shop hours are revised into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Part of the pressure over changes to shop opening times.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosphorus is the chemical element with atomic number 15.

clue.text: Commit to flames popular heretic for speaking out — consumed!

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the word for heretic is given as it is spoken

parts.note: to the church a heretic is a sinner
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A popular heretic burned at the stake for speaking his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To incinerate is to burn something completely, to consign it to fire.

clue.text: Does battle losing head and part of a rifle

parts.note: a hind is a female deer, as is a doe

indicators.note: the word for battle drops its first letter

parts.note: to battle is to fight

explanation.surface: Female deer fight on, though one is decapitated by a rifle shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb, but it is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: The hind sight is the rear sight on a rifle barrel, used with the foresight for aiming.

clue.text: Let balance dip into red, about to take advantage of charity

parts.note: the command go OD, with OD meaning overdrawn
ca, short for circa, means about
to use someone is to exploit them

explanation.surface: Someone lets their account go overdrawn so a charity can profit.
explanation.walkthrough: OD is the bank statement abbreviation for overdrawn, so go OD means let the balance go into the red.
explanation.definitionFit: A good cause is a worthy purpose that deserves support, especially a charity.

clue.text: Call round for the one with the sticks

parts.note: to ring is to telephone
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Phone and ask for the person who carries the sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer, the band member wielding drumsticks.

clue.text: For a sportsperson it would have been more hazardous to have run one at the start

indicators.note: the clue imagines the answer with extra letters that it does not actually have
the extra letters the answer would have needed are those of run and one
those missing letters belong at the front of the word for more hazardous

parts.note: riskier means more dangerous
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sporting comment that putting a run in early would have made things more dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a word for more hazardous minus its first two letters, which are run and one.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier is someone who takes part in the sport of skiing.

clue.text: Reds fan broadcast report on 1-0 reverse

indicators.note: in an across clue, report on something places report after it
the words for the score are read backwards

parts.note: a score of one-nil read out as one and the letter O

indicators.note: the word for report is given by its sound, as if aired

parts.note: to file a report is to submit it

explanation.surface: A Liverpool supporter's radio summary of a narrow 1-0 defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reds fan' suggests a football supporter, but the reds are wines.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a lover and connoisseur of wine, and red wine is a classic object of that passion.

clue.text: Welcome back occasional elegant adult learner to be graded

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: the word for occasional is turned the other way

parts.note: rare means infrequent
chic means stylish

explanation.surface: A school greets back an adult student who drops in now and then, ready to be assessed.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarchical system is one arranged in ranks or levels, one above another.

clue.text: Back to front, managed to enter expensive bar

indicators.note: the back end of the phrase is moved to the front

parts.note: got in means succeeded in entering

explanation.surface: Someone sneaked in through the back to reach a pricey bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but it is a bar of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a cast bar of metal, often gold, and so very costly.

clue.text: That is going to time, visiting sick

indicators.note: the time letter goes in to stay within the word for sick

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A timed visit to someone who is ill.
explanation.definitionFit: It'll is the contraction of it will, which expresses that something is going to happen.

clue.text: Macs grouped together and left in lavatory

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the lavatory word

parts.note: can is American slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Raincoats bundled together and abandoned in a toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Macs look like raincoats, but they are Scots whose surnames begin Mac.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a Scottish kinship group, many of whose members bear Mac surnames.

clue.text: Some paper, off-white, with no heading

indicators.note: the colour word loses its first letter

parts.note: cream is a pale yellowish white

explanation.surface: A stationer describes some untitled sheets of paper in an off-white shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a quantity of paper sheets, traditionally five hundred.

clue.text: It's critical stir-crazy daughter is kept in

indicators.note: the daughter's letter is held inside the prison and madness words

parts.note: stir and jug are both slang for prison
mental is informal for mad

explanation.surface: A girl going mad from confinement is in a serious state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir-crazy' reads as one idea, but the two halves are clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Judgmental means quick to find fault, which is one sense of critical.

clue.text: Support opera's return

indicators.note: the possessive opera name comes back the other way

parts.note: the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera, with the possessive adding S

explanation.surface: Fans back an opera company's comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A stem is the stalk that holds up a flower, so it serves as a support.

clue.text: Collapsed on tenth lap in this challenge

indicators.note: the letters of on tenth lap fall into disorder and are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete collapsed on the tenth lap of a gruelling event.
explanation.definitionFit: The pentathlon is a five-event athletic contest, a demanding test that includes running laps.
